text: a semisimple Lie subalgebra of 𝔤𝔩(V) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero contains the semisimple and nilpotent parts of each element, so faithful representations preserve the abstract Jordan decomposition (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras*, §6.4).

name: The dual Jacobi–Trudi identity
text: s_μ = det(e_{μ′ᵢ − i + j}) in the elementary symmetric polynomials over any commutative ring, the half left open when the Jacobi–Trudi identity was announced (Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, I (3.5)).

name: Symplectic transvections generate the symplectic group
text: over every field, in any characteristic, the symplectic transvections generate Sp_{2m}(K) (Artin, *Geometric Algebra*, Ch. III).

name: Topological generators of tori
text: every compact connected abelian Lie group has an element generating a dense subgroup, and such generators form a dense set (Bröcker–tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, I.4.14).

name: Lakshmibai–Seshadri paths
text: Littelmann's encoding of the LS paths of shape λ by decreasing chains of Weyl-group cosets and rational times satisfying the a-chain condition, finitely many for each λ (Littelmann, *Invent. Math.* 116 (1994)).

name: Killing vector fields
text: vector fields X with L_X g = 0, characterised by skew-adjointness of ∇X, with ∇²X = R(·, X)· and the restriction of X to any geodesic a Jacobi field (Petersen, *Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 8).

name: Stable distributions
text: the probability laws on ℝ with the stable characteristic function of index α ∈ (0, 2], skewness |β| ≤ 1, scale and location, in Nolan's S₀ parametrisation (Nolan, *Univariate Stable Distributions*, Ch. 1).

name: Borel–Moore homology
text: the homology of locally finite singular chains with local coefficients, agreeing with ordinary homology on compact spaces (Bredon, *Sheaf Theory*, Ch. V).

name: The affine Weyl group
text: the group generated by the affine reflections s_{α,k} of a root pairing, whose elements are exactly the affine maps with linear part in W and translation in the coroot lattice, W_aff = Q^∨ ⋊ W (Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, §4.2).

name: The group Spinᶜ
text: Spinᶜ(Q) = (Spin(Q) × U(1))/{±1}, with its determinant map to U(1) and its map to SO(Q), the kernel of their product being of order two (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, App. D).

name: The fundamental group of a graph of groups
text: Serre's π₁(𝔸, T): the free product of the vertex groups and the free group on the edges, modulo the edge relations and the edges of T (Serre, *Trees*, I §5.1).

name: Hirzebruch's multiplicative sequences
text: the polynomials K_k in the elementary symmetric functions with Σ K_k = ∏ Q(xᵢ) for a power series Q, multiplicative on disjoint unions of roots (Hirzebruch, *Topological Methods in Algebraic Geometry*, §1).

name: The Turing jump
text: Z′ = {e : the e-th Z-computable program halts on input e}, with Z <_T Z′ and every Z-c.e. set one-one reducible to Z′ (Soare, *Recursively Enumerable Sets and Degrees*, III.2).

name: The lemniscate constant
text: ϖ = 2∫₀¹ dt/√(1 − t⁴), the half-length of the lemniscate, with the closed form ϖ = Γ(1/4)²/(2√(2π)) (Borwein–Borwein, *Pi and the AGM*, Ch. 1).
Correctly stated: every finite abelian extension of ℚ embeds in some ℚ(ζₙ), n ≠ 0 (Washington, Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields, Thm 14.1; Wikipedia); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: π_{n+1}(Γ K, 0) ≃ H_{n+1}(K) for a nonnegatively graded chain complex of R-modules, natural in chain maps (Goerss–Jardine, Simplicial Homotopy Theory, Cor. III.2.7); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: π₀(Γ K) ≃ H₀(K) (Goerss–Jardine III.2.7); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: with [1], …, [n] units, the unique idempotent of augmentation 1 killed on both sides by every eᵢ, the Jones–Wenzl projection (Wenzl 1987; Kauffman–Lins, Temperley–Lieb Recoupling Theory, Ch. 3); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for p + q ≥ 2 the image of Spin(p, q) → SO(p, q) is the identity component SO₀(p, q) (Lawson–Michelsohn, Spin Geometry, I §2; Wikipedia, Spin group, indefinite signature); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: over an algebraically closed field, G / R_u(G) is a torus for a reduced connected solvable affine group of finite type (Borel, Linear Algebraic Groups, Thm 10.6(1); Humphreys 19.3(a)); the docstring claims no splitting G = T ⋉ G_u; compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: in the Black–Scholes market with physical drift μ, callValue at S_u equals e^{−r(T−u)} E_Q[(S_T − K)⁺ | ℱ_u] Q-a.s. under the Girsanov-tilted risk-neutral measure (Shreve, Stochastic Calculus for Finance II, §§5.2.4–5.2.5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: on a closed manifold, PSC metrics joined by a path of PSC metrics continuous in the chart C² topology are concordant (Gromov–Lawson, Ann. of Math. 111 (1980), Lemma 3); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: Newton above Hodge for a matrix with a Smith normal form over a ring with a nonnegative valuation, finite v(det A) (Kedlaya, A little p-adic numerical analysis, §3 Thm 16); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: the slope-data form of Newton above Hodge (Kedlaya, A little p-adic numerical analysis, §3 Thm 16); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: the Newton polygon of det(1 − XA) at n is Σ v(sᵢ), the Hodge endpoint (Kedlaya, §3 Thm 16); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: κ(G) ≤ λ(G) for every simple graph, Whitney's inequality (Diestel, Graph Theory, Prop. 1.4.2; Whitney 1932); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: PGL(2, K) is sharply 3-transitive on P¹(K), normalised at (0, 1, ∞) (Wikipedia, Projective linear group; Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, Ch. 3 §3.3 for K = ℂ); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the three roots of (X + 16)³ − jX are the twelfth powers of the level-two Siegel functions, Weber's identities (𝔣²⁴ − 16)³ = j𝔣²⁴, (𝔣ᵢ²⁴ + 16)³ = j𝔣ᵢ²⁴ in Siegel-function form (Wikipedia, Weber modular function; Cox, Primes of the Form x² + ny², §12); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the nuclear operators E → F with the nuclear norm, the quotient of E* ⊗̂π F by the kernel of the canonical map (Ryan, Introduction to Tensor Products of Banach Spaces, Ch. 2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: B ⊆ A whose leading terms generate the initial algebra of A (Robbiano–Sweedler 1990; Sturmfels, Gröbner Bases and Convex Polytopes, Ch. 11); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the group presented on simple classes by [S][T] = [U] whenever Hom(U, S ⊗ T) ≠ 0, the universal grading group (EGNO, Tensor Categories, §4.14); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: some resolvent is a compact operator, equivalently every one (Kato, Perturbation Theory for Linear Operators, III §6.8; Reed–Simon IV, XIII.14); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: chart-locally induced by an adic morphism of Huber pairs (Huber, Math. Z. 217 (1994), §3), with the analytic-points characterisation Prop. 3.2(ii); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: H^k_c(E) = 0 for k ≠ dim E on a finite-dimensional real normed space, the vanishing half of the Poincaré lemma for compact supports (Bott–Tu, §4; Lee, Thm 17.28); the top degree is a separate statement, as the docstring says; compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: Grothendieck's inequality for bounded bilinear forms on C(K) × C(L) with the constant 16, not sharp, as the docstring says (Albiac–Kalton, Topics in Banach Space Theory, 8.1.3); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: Menger's theorem, internally vertex-disjoint paths, for multigraphs with finitely many vertices (Menger 1927; Schrijver, Combinatorial Optimization, §9.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: the undirected max-flow/min-cut theorem for nonnegative edge capacities on a multigraph (Ford–Fulkerson, Flows in Networks, Ch. I); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the Littlewood–Richardson rule with c^ν_{λμ} the number of Littlewood–Richardson tableaux of shape ν/λ and content μ (Fulton, Young Tableaux, §5.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the Littlewood–Richardson rule for rational Weyl modules of GLₙ(ℂ) indexed by arbitrary dominant weights, via determinant twists (Fulton–Harris, Lecture 6 and §15.5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: flasque sheaves of modules have Extⁿ⁺¹(R_U, F) = 0, so are acyclic (Hartshorne, Prop. III.2.5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the stable category of Gorenstein-projective objects of an abelian category embeds fully faithfully into D^b(C)/Perf(C) (X.-W. Chen, Math. Nachr. 284 (2011), Thm 2.1); the docstring claims only the fully faithful half of Buchweitz; compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the lattice glued from a row of the rootful rank-24 table along its glue code (Conway–Sloane, SPLAG, Ch. 16 §1, Table 16.1); unimodularity is proved for 19 rows and labelled so; compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

name: The Kronecker–Weber theorem
text: every finite abelian extension of ℚ embeds in a cyclotomic field ℚ(ζₙ) (Washington, *Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields*, Thm 14.1).

name: Homotopy groups under Dold–Kan
text: for a nonnegatively graded chain complex K of R-modules, the homotopy groups of the simplicial module Γ(K) are the homology groups of K, π₀ included, naturally in chain maps (Goerss–Jardine, *Simplicial Homotopy Theory*, III.2.7).

name: Jones–Wenzl projections
text: when the quantum integers [1], …, [n] are invertible, the Temperley–Lieb algebra TLₙ(δ) has exactly one idempotent of augmentation 1 killed on both sides by every generator eᵢ, given by Wenzl's recursion (Wenzl, *C. R. Math. Rep. Acad. Sci. Canada* 9 (1987)).

name: The image of Spin(p, q) is SO₀(p, q)
text: for p + q ≥ 2 the image of Spin(p, q) → SO(p, q) is the identity component SO₀(p, q), the kernel of the spinor norm, so with the kernel {±1} announced earlier Spin(p, q) double covers SO₀(p, q) (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, I §2).

name: The unipotent part of a connected solvable group
text: over an algebraically closed field, in every characteristic, the unipotent points of a connected solvable linear algebraic group are exactly the points of its unipotent radical, and the quotient by it is a torus (Borel, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, Thm 10.6(1)).

name: The Black–Scholes formula as a conditional risk-neutral price
text: in the Black–Scholes market with physical drift μ, the call and put prices at the spot S_u are the discounted conditional expected payoffs e^{−r(T−u)} E_Q[· | ℱ_u] under the Girsanov risk-neutral measure Q, extending the static formula of TauCeti#18827 (Shreve, *Stochastic Calculus for Finance II*, §5.2.4).

name: Isotopic metrics of positive scalar curvature are concordant
text: on a closed manifold M, PSC metrics joined by a C²-continuous path of PSC metrics are concordant: some PSC metric on M × ℝ equals g₀ + dt² for t ≤ 0 and g₁ + dt² for t ≥ 1 (Gromov–Lawson, *Ann. of Math.* 111 (1980), Lemma 3).

name: Newton above Hodge
text: for a matrix over a ring with a nonnegative valuation, such as a lattice endomorphism over a DVR, the Hodge polygon of its invariant factors lies on or below the Newton polygon of det(1 − XA), with the same endpoint (Kedlaya, *A little p-adic numerical analysis*, Thm 16).

name: Whitney's inequality
text: for a simple graph, κ(G) ≤ λ(G) ≤ δ(G): the vertex connectivity is at most the edge connectivity, which is at most the minimum degree once the graph is finite with at least two vertices (Diestel, *Graph Theory*, Prop. 1.4.2).

name: Sharp triple transitivity of Möbius transformations
text: over any field K exactly one element of PGL(2, K) carries 0, 1, ∞ to three given distinct points of the projective line, and over an algebraically closed K exactly one element of PSL(2, K) (Ahlfors, *Complex Analysis*, Ch. 3 §3.3).

name: Weber's cubic
text: the twelfth powers of the level-two Siegel functions g_{(0,1/2)}, g_{(1/2,0)}, g_{(1/2,1/2)} are the three roots of (X + 16)³ = jX, Weber's identities (𝔣²⁴ − 16)³ = j𝔣²⁴ and (𝔣ᵢ²⁴ + 16)³ = j𝔣ᵢ²⁴ in Siegel-function form (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §12).

name: Nuclear operators
text: for Banach spaces E, F, the image of E* ⊗̂π F → L(E, F), a Banach space under the nuclear norm ν inherited from the projective tensor product, with ν(A∘T∘B) ≤ ‖A‖ ν(T) ‖B‖; also being formalised in mathlib4#42197 (Ryan, *Introduction to Tensor Products of Banach Spaces*, Ch. 2).

name: SAGBI bases
text: for a monomial order, the initial algebra of a subalgebra A ⊆ k[x₁, …, xₙ] is generated by the leading terms of A, and a SAGBI basis of A is a subset whose leading terms generate the initial algebra (Sturmfels, *Gröbner Bases and Convex Polytopes*, Ch. 11).

name: The universal grading group
text: the group U(C) presented on the simple objects of a tensor category C by [S][T] = [U] whenever U occurs in S ⊗ T, through which every group grading of C factors (EGNO, *Tensor Categories*, §4.14).

name: Operators with compact resolvent
text: an unbounded operator A has compact resolvent when some (λ − A)⁻¹ is a compact operator, hence all are; for self-adjoint D the bounded inverse (1 + D²)⁻¹ = R(i)*R(i) is then a positive compact operator (Kato, *Perturbation Theory for Linear Operators*, III §6.8).

name: Adic morphisms of adic spaces
text: morphisms chart-locally induced by adic homomorphisms of Huber pairs; a morphism of adic spaces is adic exactly when it sends analytic points to analytic points (Huber, *Math. Z.* 217 (1994), §3, Prop. 3.2).

name: Von Neumann's density theorem
text: an operator in the double commutant of a unital ⋆-subalgebra of the bounded operators on a Hilbert space is a strong-operator limit of elements of the subalgebra (Kadison–Ringrose, *Fundamentals of the Theory of Operator Algebras*, Thm 5.3.1).

name: The Perron–Frobenius theorem
text: now in full: an irreducible nonnegative real matrix has a positive eigenvector whose eigenvalue is positive, simple and equal to the spectral radius, and every nonnegative eigenvector is a multiple of it (Seneta, *Non-negative Matrices and Markov Chains*, Thm 1.5).

name: The Kronecker–Weber theorem, with the conductor
text: the least n with a given finite abelian extension of ℚ inside ℚ(ζₙ) is the finite part of its conductor, sharpening TauCeti#24374 (Washington, *Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields*, Ch. 3).

name: The Harish-Chandra isomorphism
text: for a split semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the Harish-Chandra projection is an algebra isomorphism from the centre of U(𝔤) onto the dot-action invariants S(𝔥)^{W·}; injective here, onto in TauCeti#24546 (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §23.3).

name: The structure theorem for Iwasawa modules
text: every finitely generated module over O⟦X⟧, O a complete discrete valuation ring, is pseudo-isomorphic to O⟦X⟧ʳ ⊕ ⨁ᵢ O⟦X⟧/(ϖ^{mᵢ}) ⊕ ⨁ⱼ O⟦X⟧/(Fⱼ^{nⱼ}) with the Fⱼ irreducible distinguished polynomials (Washington, *Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields*, Thm 13.12).

name: The Bochner formula
text: for a smooth function f on a Riemannian manifold, Δ|∇f|² = 2|Hess f|² + 2⟨∇f, ∇Δf⟩ + 2 Ric(∇f, ∇f) (Petersen, *Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 9).

name: The étale fundamental group of a field is its absolute Galois group
text: for a separable closure Ω of K, the group Gal(Ω/K), acting on geometric fibres at Spec Ω → Spec K, is the fundamental group of the Galois category of finite étale K-schemes (SGA 1, Exp. V, Prop. 8.1).

name: Galois descent for modules
text: for a finite group G acting freely on a ring B with invariants A, B ⊗_A N^G ≅ N for every B-module N with semilinear G-action, and M ≅ (B ⊗_A M)^G for every A-module M (Chase–Harrison–Rosenberg 1965).

name: Deligne's theorem on integral modular forms
text: a polynomial in the coefficients a₁, …, a₆ of the universal Weierstrass equation is an integral modular form of weight k exactly when it is weighted homogeneous of weight k and lies in ℤ[c₄, c₆, Δ] (Deligne, *Courbes elliptiques: formulaire*, 1975).

name: The Euler characteristic of the Khovanov complex is the Jones polynomial
text: for an oriented link diagram, the graded Euler characteristic of the cohomology of its Khovanov bracket is, up to the normalising shifts, (q + q⁻¹) times the Jones polynomial (Khovanov, *Duke Math. J.* 101 (2000)).

name: The Kechris–Solecki–Todorcevic G₀ dichotomy
text: a graph on a Polish space with analytic edge relation either has a Borel colouring with countably many colours or admits a continuous homomorphism from G₀, and never both (Kechris–Solecki–Todorcevic, *Adv. Math.* 141 (1999)).

name: A low simple set
text: there is a computably enumerable set that is simple and low, so its Turing degree lies strictly between the computable degree and the halting degree (Soare, *Recursively Enumerable Sets and Degrees*, Thm VII.1.1).

name: Uniform convexity of Lᵖ
text: now for all 1 < p < ∞: Lᵖ(μ; E) is uniformly convex whenever E is, hence reflexive when E is complete, extending the range 2 ≤ p of TauCeti#20699 (Day, *Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.* 47 (1941)).

name: The Fourier inversion theorem for characteristic functions
text: a finite measure on a finite-dimensional inner product space whose characteristic function is integrable is absolutely continuous, with density the inverse Fourier transform of the characteristic function (Feller, *An Introduction to Probability Theory* II, XV.3).

name: Schauder's theorem
text: a bounded operator from a normed space into a Banach space over ℝ or ℂ is compact if and only if its adjoint is compact (Conway, *A Course in Functional Analysis*, VI.3.4).

name: The affine Weyl group acts simply transitively on alcoves
text: for a point x on no affine root hyperplane, exactly one element of the affine Weyl group carries the fundamental alcove onto the alcove of x (Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, §4.5).

name: Alexander's trick
text: a homeomorphism of the closed unit ball of a real normed space fixing the unit sphere is isotopic to the identity through homeomorphisms fixing the sphere (Farb–Margalit, *A Primer on Mapping Class Groups*, Lemma 2.1).

name: The elementary renewal theorem
text: for a renewal process with i.i.d. nonnegative increments not almost surely zero, the expected number of renewals by time t satisfies m(t)/t → 1/𝔼T, with limit 0 when the mean is infinite (Feller, *An Introduction to Probability Theory* II, XI.1).

name: Ocneanu's trace
text: for every parameter z there is exactly one Markov trace with parameter z on the infinite type-A Hecke algebra over a commutative ring, the trace behind Jones's construction of the HOMFLY polynomial (Jones, *Ann. of Math.* 126 (1987), Thm 5.1).

name: Chevalley's theorem on coinvariants
text: for a finite group generated by pseudoreflections, of order invertible in the field, Sym(V*) is a free module over the invariants, and for a faithful action the coinvariant algebra has dimension |G| (Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, §3.6).

name: The Singer–Wermer theorem
text: a bounded derivation of a commutative complex Banach algebra, unital or not, takes its values in the Jacobson radical (Singer–Wermer 1955; Dales, *Banach Algebras and Automatic Continuity*, Thm 2.7.20).

name: Capelli's theorem
text: over any field, Xⁿ − a is irreducible exactly when a is not a p-th power for any prime p dividing n and, when 4 ∣ n, a is not of the form −4b⁴; Mathlib had the odd-degree case (Lang, *Algebra*, VI Thm 9.1).

name: The Stieltjes inversion formula
text: a finite measure μ on ℝ is recovered from its Stieltjes transform m(z) = ∫ (x − z)⁻¹ dμ(x): as η → 0⁺, π⁻¹ ∫ₐᵇ Im m(x + iη) dx → μ(a, b) + ½ μ{a} + ½ μ{b} (Anderson–Guionnet–Zeitouni, *An Introduction to Random Matrices*, Thm 2.4.3).

name: Grothendieck's Galois theory of finite étale covers
text: now in full: over any connected scheme the finite étale schemes form a Galois category, with the geometric fibre at any geometric point as a fibre functor; TauCeti#23181 had affine bases (SGA 1, Exp. V, §7).

name: The free central limit theorem
text: for freely independent centred elements with uniformly bounded moments and average variance tending to σ², the moments of N^{−1/2}(a₁ + ⋯ + a_N) converge to those of the semicircle law of variance σ² (Nica–Speicher, *Lectures on the Combinatorics of Free Probability*, Thm 8.10).

name: The model existence theorem
text: a countable member of a consistency property for L_{ω₁ω} over a countable language has a countable model in which every element is named by a Henkin constant (Keisler, *Model Theory for Infinitary Logic*; Marker, *Lectures on Infinitary Model Theory*, §4.1).

name: Cohen–Macaulay rings are universally catenary
text: a Noetherian ring whose localisations at all primes are Cohen–Macaulay is universally catenary (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 17.9).

name: Any two fibre functors of a Galois category are isomorphic
text: every natural transformation between fibre functors of a Galois category is an isomorphism, and between any two fibre functors there is one (SGA 1, Exp. V, §5).

name: The Poincaré lemma for compactly supported cohomology
text: now in full: for an n-dimensional real vector space E, H^k_c(E) vanishes for k ≠ n and integration against an orientation is an isomorphism H^n_c(E) ≅ ℝ (Bott–Tu, *Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology*, Cor. 4.7).

name: Turing degrees form an upper semilattice
text: the Turing join f ⊕ g is reducible to h exactly when both f and g are, so any two Turing degrees have a least upper bound; Mathlib has the partial order (Soare, *Recursively Enumerable Sets and Degrees*, I.4).

name: Computably inseparable sets exist
text: the sets {e : φₑ(e) = 0} and {e : φₑ(e) = 1} are disjoint computably enumerable sets that no computable set separates (Soare, *Recursively Enumerable Sets and Degrees*, I.3).

name: Theta series of even unimodular lattices are polynomials in E₄ and Δ
text: the theta series of an even unimodular lattice of rank 2k is a unique rational linear combination of the products E₄ᵃ Δᵇ with 4a + 12b = k (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII §6).

name: Witt's example: the theta series does not determine the lattice
text: the even unimodular lattices E₈ ⊕ E₈ and D₁₆⁺ have the same theta series E₄² but are not isometric (Conway–Sloane, *Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups*, Ch. 4).

name: Mertens' second theorem for number fields
text: for a number field K, the sum of 1/N𝔭 over the nonzero prime ideals of norm at most x is log log x + B_K + O(1/log x) (Rosen, *J. Ramanujan Math. Soc.* 14 (1999)).

name: Koteljanskii's inequality
text: for a positive semidefinite matrix A and index sets S, T, det A[S ∪ T] · det A[S ∩ T] ≤ det A[S] · det A[T], which contains the Hadamard–Fischer inequality (Horn–Johnson, *Matrix Analysis*, §7.8).

name: Roby's theorem on divided powers
text: for a free module M over a commutative ring, γ_d(m) ↦ m^{⊗d} is an isomorphism from the degree-d part of the divided power algebra Γ(M) onto the symmetric tensors in M^{⊗d} (Roby, *Ann. Sci. ENS* 80 (1963), Thm IV.2).

name: Pratelli's theorem
text: for an atomless source measure and a continuous cost on standard Borel spaces, the Monge infimum over transport maps equals the Kantorovich infimum over couplings, whether finite or not (Pratelli, *Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Probab. Statist.* 43 (2007), Thm B).

name: Mal'cev's theorem
text: a finitely generated residually finite group is Hopfian: every surjective endomorphism is injective (Robinson, *A Course in the Theory of Groups*, 6.1.12).

name: Narayana numbers count noncrossing partitions by blocks
text: the noncrossing partitions of an n-element linearly ordered set into k blocks number (1/n)·C(n, k)·C(n, k − 1) (Kreweras, *Discrete Math.* 1 (1972)).

name: Quaternionic differentiability is rigid
text: a function ℍ → ℍ whose left difference quotients converge at every point of a connected open set is of the form q ↦ a + q·b there, and conversely (Sudbery, *Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc.* 85 (1979), Thm 1).

name: Geometrically reduced extensions are separably generated
text: a finitely generated field extension that is geometrically reduced has a transcendence basis over which it is separable algebraic, the converse of Mac Lane's criterion left open in Mathlib (Stacks 030W).

name: The Hilbert class field
text: the ray class field K_𝔪 of a modulus 𝔪, with Cl_𝔪(K) ≅ Gal(K_𝔪/K) by the Artin map; the Hilbert class field H is the case 𝔪 = 1, with Cl(K) ≅ Gal(H/K) and [H : K] = h_K (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI.6).

name: Algebraic spaces
text: a presheaf on schemes that is an fppf sheaf, has representable diagonal, and admits a surjective étale atlas by a scheme (Stacks 025Y).

name: Ample line bundles
text: a line bundle class on a quasi-compact scheme is ample when the affine nonvanishing loci of sections of its positive powers cover; the structure sheaf is ample exactly when the scheme is quasi-affine (Stacks 01PS).

name: Integral perfectoid rings
text: a ring that is π-adically complete for some π with πᵖ dividing p, whose Frobenius is surjective modulo p, and whose Fontaine map θ has principal kernel (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, *Integral p-adic Hodge theory*, Def. 3.5).

name: The full crossed product
text: the C*-algebra A ⋊_α G of a C*-dynamical system, the completion of the twisted convolution algebra C_c(G, A) in the universal norm (Williams, *Crossed Products of C*-Algebras*, Ch. 2).

name: Borel reducibility and smooth equivalence relations
text: E ≤_B F when a Borel map f satisfies E(x, y) ↔ F(f x, f y); E is smooth when it reduces to equality on Cantor space, and the eventual-equality relation E₀ is not smooth (Gao, *Invariant Descriptive Set Theory*, Ch. 5).

name: The symplectization of a contact form
text: the one-form eᵗα on ℝ × M, whose exterior derivative is nondegenerate exactly when α is a contact form (Geiges, *An Introduction to Contact Topology*, Ch. 1).

name: The ring class field of an order

## What it says
`IsAlgebraicSpace F` says that a presheaf of sets `F` on the category of schemes is an *algebraic space* in the sense of the Stacks Project: an fppf sheaf whose diagonal is representable by schemes and which has an étale atlas.

- It is a `structure ... : Prop`, a proposition with three fields, all required.
  - `isSheaf`: `F` is a sheaf for `Scheme.fppfTopology`, Mathlib's topology on schemes generated by the jointly surjective families of flat morphisms locally of finite presentation.
  - `representableDiagonal`: `RepresentableDiagonal F`, that is `yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (diag F)`: for every scheme `T` and morphism `h_T ⟶ F ⨯ F`, its fibre product with the diagonal `F ⟶ F ⨯ F` is represented by a scheme. By Mathlib's `Functor.relativelyRepresentable.diag_iff`, this says that every morphism `h_U ⟶ F` from a scheme is representable.
  - `exists_etaleAtlas`: there are a scheme `U` and a morphism `a : h_U ⟶ F` with `EtaleAtlas a`, that is `MorphismProperty.presheaf @Etale a` and `MorphismProperty.presheaf @Surjective a`: `a` is representable, and its base change along every `h_T ⟶ F` from a scheme is an étale, respectively surjective, morphism of schemes.

This is Definition 65.6.1 of the Stacks Project condition by condition: (1) the fppf sheaf condition, (2) the representable diagonal, (3) a surjective étale morphism from a scheme, "surjective" and "étale" for a transformation meaning, as there, representable with all base changes so. The one difference is the base: the Stacks Project works over a base scheme $S$; here the site is the category of all schemes, as the roadmap target asks.

The automorphism group of an elliptic curve over an integral domain is finite, in every characteristic.

This is the finiteness in Silverman, Theorem III.10.1, that $\mathrm{Aut}(E)$ is a finite group (of order dividing $24$).
